articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Could Viktor Gyökeres leave Arsenal in January?
articles.description: Arsenal forward Viktor Gyökeres could leave the club in January, while Manchester United are looking to bolster their squad in January. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂とニュース：ヴィクトル・ギョケレスは1月にアーセナルを去るのか？
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナルのフォワード、ヴィクトル・ギョケレスが1月に退団する可能性がある一方、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは1月の補強を模索している。最新の移籍情報をお届けする。
articles.body:
Arsenal forward Viktor Gyökeres could leave the club in January, while Manchester United are looking to bolster their squad in January after criticism over their level of investment from defender Lisandro Martínez.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Viktor Gyökeres is prepared to leave Arsenal in January for more consistent game time, claims TEAMtalk. The report states that frustration over a lack of minutes has forced the Sweden international to consider his future with the Gunners, just over a year on from his initial £55 million move from Sporting CP. The 28-year-old has been restricted to three Premier League appearances so far this season, all from the bench, despite scoring 21 goals for Arsenal across all competitions last campaign. Atletico Madrid have been labelled as an interested party, while teams in Italy, Germany, and Spain have also been outlined as possible destinations.

- Liverpool are showing keen interest in Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu as an option for the January transfer window, according to Football Insider. The 26-year-old is being tracked by the Merseyside outfit as an option to bolster the backline, with his ability to play as both a centre-back and a right back viewed as highly desirable. Kalulu has a deal until 2029 with Juventus, and has featured in every game this season, suggesting any transfer could be difficult to secure.

 

- Manchester United are ready to dip into the January transfer market to bolster the backline amid concerns over the quality in the defensive ranks. Sky Sports reports that the club is looking at center backs and left backs who could make an impact, after spending the two previous summers improving the forward line and the midfield. It's unclear exactly what funds could be available to the recruitment team, amid growing pressure to improve after a difficult start to the season.

- Arsenal and Chelsea are both tracking the progress of Oliver Mansson, 17, during a breakthrough campaign for IFK Goteborg. That's according to TEAMtalk, who claim the midfielder has caught the eye of the two Premier League clubs, along with a whole host of other English clubs. Mansson has featured 17 times across all competitions this season, 13 of which have been in the Allsvenskan. The youngster has a deal until 2028 with Goteborg, which could prompt a move in the future, though he cannot officially move to the Premier League until next August, when he would turn 18.

- AC Milan are monitoring defensive options for the January transfer window, with Matteo Gabbia set to miss at least three months of action with a torn hamstring. Calciomercato reports contact has already been made with Gonçalo Inácio, 25, as an option, though Sporting CP will demand over €40 million for an exit. Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae is another potential option, with less than two years remaining on his contract.

articles.headline: Fairbairn's last-second 49-yard FG gives Texans 34-31 win over Jaguars at Wembley Stadium
articles.description: — Trying to seal a desperately needed win, Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw an interception in the end zone and gave the Jacksonville Jaguars another chance on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: フェアバーンの終了間際の49ヤードFGにより、テキサンズがウェンブリー・スタジアムでジャガーズに34-31で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: どうしても勝利が必要な状況の中、ヒューストン・テキサンズのクォーターバック、C.J.ストラウドがエンドゾーン内でインターセプトを投げてしまい、日曜日の試合でジャクソンビル・ジャガーズに逆転のチャンスを与えてしまった。
articles.body:
LONDON -- — Trying to seal a desperately needed win, Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw an interception in the end zone and gave the Jacksonville Jaguars another chance on Sunday.


              Jacksonville tied the game at 31-31, but Stroud didn't stress about it.


              “His mindset was 'Hey, I got you Coach, don’t worry about it,” Houston coach DeMeco Ryans said.


              With just under two minutes left, Stroud led a drive to set up Ka’imi Fairbairn's 49-yard field goal as time expired and the Texans won 34-31 on the slick grass of Wembley Stadium.


              “When a player tells me that, that just gives me the confidence that I need,” Ryans said. “He responded in an outstanding way.”


              Stroud threw three touchdown passes and Marvin Harrison Jr. made his debut for the Texans (2-4) as Houston earned back-to-back wins to gain ground on the AFC South-leading Jaguars (4-2).


              Cam Little’s 60-yard field goal had tied the game — a week after his 57-yarder won it for Jacksonville against the Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium — after Travis Hunter intercepted Stroud’s pass in the end zone.


              Hunter also hauled in a 7-yard touchdown pass at the other end — becoming just the fifth player in the Super Bowl era, including the playoffs, to both score a touchdown and intercept a pass in the same game.


              “Just made a mistake,” Stroud said of Hunter's pick. “I've learned in my life I've got to flush my failures and flush my successes and just move on. Our defense did a great job holding them to three points, and then gave me the ball back, and went down and had a game-winning drive.”


              Stroud said he appreciated hearing words of support from Ryans and his teammates.


              “What they did for me in that moment really meant a lot,” he said.


              Tight end Foster Moreau caught two touchdown passes from Stroud, who also connected with Jaylin Noel for a 13-yard score in the third quarter for a 24-14 lead.


              Moreau scored on a 6-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter and a 1-yarder just before the end of the half.


              Penalties dogged the Jaguars for a third straight week. They were flagged for too many men on the field on a Houston punt — extending a Texans drive that ended with Noel’s touchdown.


              Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes, including a pair to Bhayshul Tuten. His 1-yard pass to rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher cut Houston’s lead to 24-21.


              Houston responded with Jawhar Jordan’s 25-yard touchdown run to restore a 10-point lead, 31-21, late in the third quarter.


              Two-way star Hunter, who scored his first NFL touchdown at Wembley a year ago, snagged his second when he hauled in a pass over the middle to reduce Houston’s lead to 31-28 in the fourth quarter.

articles.headline: Ruben Amorim still unbeaten in Serie A after Milan win
articles.description: AC Milan held off a fightback from Atalanta to close out a 3-2 win at San Siro and move up into fourth in Serie A with manager Ruben Amorim remaining unbeaten in his first seven league games.
articles.headlineJa: ルーベン・アモリム、ミラン勝利によりセリエAで無敗を維持
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランはサン・シーロでアタランタの反撃を凌ぎ切り3-2で勝利。セリエAで4位に浮上し、監督のルーベン・アモリムはリーグ戦最初の7試合で無敗を継続している。
articles.body:
AC Milan held off a fightback from Atalanta to close out a 3-2 win at San Siro and move up into fourth in Serie A with manager Ruben Amorim remaining unbeaten in his first seven league games.

The Rossoneri, who had won 4-0 away at RB Salzburg in the Europa League on Thursday night, took the lead through Goncalo Ramos' penalty, with Adrien Rabiot slotting in a second just before the break.

Ramos then saw another spot kick saved, but Mario Gila made it 3-0 on the hour, before Atalanta fought back with goals from Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic, however, they could not find an equaliser.

Christian Pulisic saw his early goal from close range ruled out for a tight offside call following a VAR check.

Milan then did get themselves in front after 24 minutes.

Atalanta substitute Relja Obric, who had not long been sent on for his league debut to replace injured defender Sead Kolasinac, turned to block Yunus Musah's shot, but the ball struck his outstretched hand.

After reviewing the incident on the pitchside monitor, the referee awarded a penalty, which Ramos coolly dispatched by sending Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi the wrong way.

Milan doubled their lead just before halftime when Diego Moreira found Rabiot at the edge of the area and he cut inside before drilling a low shot back into the bottom corner.

The home side was awarded another penalty in the 56th minute following a VAR review after a handball by Thomas Kristensen from Rabiot's volley. Carnesecchi, though, this time guessed right to parry Ramos' spot kick.

From the resulting corner, Gila headed in at the back post off Rabiot's flick-on to seemingly put the result beyond doubt.

Atalanta, though, rallied after substitute Gaetano showed neat control in the six-yard box to pull a goal back in the 66th minute and then Krstovic further reduced the deficit after a swift counter attack with nine minutes left, but Ruben Amorim's side dug in to see out the closing stages.

Milan, led by former Manchester United coach Amorim, are one of four teams undefeated in Serie A, along with rival Inter Milan, Lazio and Roma.

Information from PA and The Associated Press was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Noni Madueke sinks Nottingham Forest with Arsenal's only shot on target
articles.description: Noni Madueke climbed off the bench to earn toothless Arsenal a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.
articles.headlineJa: ノニ・マドゥエケが唯一の枠内シュートを決め、ノッティンガム・フォレストを撃破
articles.descriptionJa: ノニ・マドゥエケがベンチから出場し、決定力に欠けたアーセナルにノッティンガム・フォレスト戦での1-0の勝利をもたらしました。
articles.body:
Noni Madueke climbed off the bench to earn toothless Arsenal a 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.

Madueke, dropped from the recent England squad, came on at half-time and his deflected effort 10 minutes from time was enough for the three points at the City Ground.

The goal was Arsenal's only shot on target in a disjointed performance that lacked attacking quality, although the champions' ability to grind out a result cannot be questioned.

The victory moved them back up to second, three points behind leaders Manchester City, but what that actually means given the wider picture of City's guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules remains to be seen.

It was a third 1-0 home defeat of the season for Forest, who are struggling to adapt to life under Oliver Glasner, and they have not scored in five home matches in all competitions after missing two big late chances.

This was also a third league defeat in a row and they now sit in the relegation zone after seven games.

It was a pedestrian first half, in which both sides sparred without showing any threat in the final third.

Forest had the first meaningful attack as a breakaway after capitalising on a Riccardo Calafiori error ended in Dan Ndoye's shot being deflected for a corner after 20 minutes.

But it was slim pickings from there as Kai Havertz headed over a Declan Rice free-kick in a dismal opening 45 minutes that yielded no shots on target.

Arteta was not impressed and replaced Eberechi Eze with Madueke at half-time in a bid to inject some more energy.

But it was Forest who began the second period invigorated as Liam Delap began to find space and he drilled a shot which was deflected into the side-netting, with Murillo then not getting enough on his header from the resulting corner.

Ndoye gave Gabriel the slip as he burst into the box, but he was unable to get his shot away.

Arteta sent for the heavy artillery midway through the second half as Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino came on.

And Arsenal should have gone ahead in the 72nd minute as they fashioned their best chance.

A slick move saw Jurriën Timber get to the byline and pull back for Rice, who slammed over the crossbar from 12 yards.

The Gunners finally upped the ante and went ahead in the 80th minute.

Rice worked the ball out to Madueke, who cut inside from the left and fired a shot which deflected off Jair Cunha and into the far corner.

Forest should have equalised in the 89th minute as they broke clear, but Chris Wood took too long to shoot and was snuffed out.

They had an even better chance deep into stoppage time as Murillo danced into the area but fizzed his shot over.

Ezri Konsa then produced a brilliant last-gasp tackle to deny Delap as the hosts could not force a leveller.

articles.headline: Diego Gómez heeds advice from Lionel Messi as Brighton follow their 'challenge the establishment' mantra
articles.description: It was a goal Lionel Messi would have been proud of. But not for the reasons you might think.
articles.headlineJa: ブライトンが「体制への挑戦」という信条を掲げる中、ディエゴ・ゴメスがリオネル・メッシのアドバイスに従う
articles.descriptionJa: それはリオネル・メッシが誇りに思うようなゴールでした。しかし、それはあなたが想像する理由からではありません。
articles.body:
BRIGHTON, England -- It was a goal Lionel Messi would have been proud of. But not for the reasons you might think.

When Diego Gómez won the ball back near the halfway line, we can presume two things would have crossed his mind. The first was that Crystal Palace goalkeeper Walter Benítez was standing considerably off his line. The second was a piece of advice he received from Messi when they were teammates at Inter Miami.

"He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear," Gómez said of the Argentine in an interview soon after joining the club.

The Paraguay international took both of these things to an extreme, lobbing Benitez from 56 yards out. The home supporters were already delirious after Jaydee Canvot's fourth-minute own-goal, and this tipped them over.

Grey clouds had dramatically burst upon the Amex moments before kickoff and, after Gómez's goal, the floodgates were opened. Yasin Ayari made it 3-0 within 10 minutes before further goals in the second half from Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood saw it finish 5-0 to the Seagulls.

Brighton have never lacked for aesthetic appeal; Graham Potter, Roberto De Zerbi and now Fabian Hürzeler have all built devastating forward lines. But this Gómez strike was of a different ilk and for those lucky to witness it in the Amex Stadium, it felt transcendental.

This feeling didn't stem from the goal's adroitness, rather its audacity. The noise went through the roof, and it felt like there was no ceiling. Suddenly, anything felt possible. The result took them provisionally into second, but finished the weekend in third after Arsenal just got past Nottingham Forest later in the afternoon.

For so long, Brighton have been held as a beacon of modernity. No conversation about the Seagulls is complete without the use of the word 'analytics.' And yet, there has always been a patronising air that borders on dismissive to the way in which they are discussed.

- Fabian Hürzeler tells Brighton fans: Have a beer and don't look at Premier League table

- Seven games, seven points: Man United are sleepwalking to another lost season

- Why do Liverpool's big-money transfers keep failing to deliver?

Some of this is because for the majority of the footballing public, eschewing the eye-test for Excel when analysing a player remains a vexing concept. Having a starting lineup composed of players that your average football fan on the street would struggle to name adds to this. The lack of an English core in the squad furthers the sense of them being an entity unto themselves.

The numbers are the narrative for a club like Brighton and often, it has felt like they have lacked the intangibles to capture one's imagination. Their recruitment models have helped them spot players like Kostoulas, who scored his fifth goal of the season on Sunday. But confidence, and dare I say, aura, can't be unearthed on spreadsheets.

articles.headlineJa: NFL第6週：日曜日の試合から得られた大きな収穫、疑問点、そしてファンタジー視点での考察
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの記者たちが、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えながら、全ての展開に反応します。第6週から得られた知見がこちらです。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars. 

Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made his much-anticipated Texans debut, but it was quarterback C.J. Stroud who was the star of this day as Houston was able to hold off the Jaguars in a thriller.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

HOU-JAX

Catch up on Thursday's game:

SEA-DEN

Houston 34, Jacksonville 31

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Texans

Can quarterback C.J. Stroud keep this hot start going? Even though Stroud did have an ill-timed interception that gave the Jaguars a chance late in the fourth quarter, he was stellar. The fourth-year quarterback is continuing to perform at an MVP level, but against the Jaguars, Houston needed him at his best -- and he delivered. He led the game-winning drive to cap a 306-yard, three-touchdown outing in his first London performance.

Trend to watch: The Texans' "elite" defense has been far from it. Coach DeMeco Ryans took over playcalling this week, but his unit allowed 31 points. It's the third time this season that the Texans have allowed at least 30 points. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: vs. Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Jaguars

Is it time for the Jaguars to fully unleash Travis Hunter on offense? They may need to. Hunter had his best offensive game of the season. He caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown after having just two catches for 17 yards in the first five games. The Jaguars needed him to step up because receiver Brian Thomas Jr. struggled, dropping two passes -- including one that would have given the Jaguars a chance to attempt a long field goal at the end of the first half. Thomas, who had an issue with drops last year, didn't play an offensive snap in the second half after playing 15 in the first. Hunter, with a bigger offensive workload, could make up for Thomas' struggles.

Trend to watch: The Jaguars are banged up at safety, with Antonio Johnson leaving the game with an ankle injury. They were already down Caleb Ransaw (IR) and went to Kaevon Merriweather, who was on the practice squad until he was signed to the active roster before last week's game. With the bye next week, the Jaguars need to get healthy and possibly make another move depending on how long Johnson is out. -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: vs. Colts (Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET)

articles.headline: Cowboys-Packers rivalry rewind: Micah Parsons' return, Dez Bryant's catch, Ice Bowl
articles.description: Their "Sunday Night Football" matchup could add another memorable chapter to Packers-Cowboys lore.
articles.body:
The history between the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys runs deep, starting with one of the NFL's most iconic games, coined the Ice Bowl.  From Hall of Fame coaches (Vince Lombardi, Tom Landry, Jimmy Johnson) to Hall of Fame players (Bart Starr, Jerry Kramer, Paul Hornung, Forrest Gregg, Reggie White, Brett Favre, Charles Woodson, Bob Lilly, Mel Renfro, Bob Hayes, Troy Aikman, Michael Irvin, Emmitt Smith) -- and likely future Hall of Famers (Aaron Rodgers, Zack Martin, Jason Witten) -- their biggest meetings are loaded with star power.

Who knows where their "Sunday Night Football" matchup will rank, but it certainly could add another chapter to one of the NFL's most storied rivalries. NFL Nation reporters Rob Demovsky and Todd Archer look back at the top moments between the Packers and Cowboys.

Parsons' homecoming ends in historic tie

Micah Parsons' return to Dallas delivered plenty of drama but no winner as the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys played to a 40-40 overtime tie in Week 4 of the 2025 season on "Sunday Night Football."

The teams combined for touchdowns on six straight second-half possessions, with Dak Prescott's 28-yard strike to George Pickens putting Dallas ahead with 43 seconds left in regulation. Jordan Love and the Packers answered by setting up Brandon McManus' 53-yard field goal to force overtime. After Brandon Aubrey's 22-yard kick gave Dallas the lead, Love kept Green Bay alive with a fourth-and-6 completion to Matthew Golden. McManus then drilled a 34-yarder with one second remaining to seal the NFL's highest-scoring tie since regular-season overtime began in 1974, according to ESPN Research.

"I felt like I was giving them my best shot, and they gave me their best shot, and then we just came out into a draw," Parsons said. "It was a 12-round fight, like on both sides. I think both sides could have played better."

The draw also kept Green Bay unbeaten at AT&T Stadium, moving the Packers to 6-0-1 there, including their Super Bowl XLV victory.

Playoffs again: Cowboys crumble in wild-card upset

When the two teams met in the wild-card round of the 2023 playoffs, the Cowboys were 12-5, unbeaten at home and heavy favorites. Meanwhile, the Packers snuck into the playoffs at 9-8 with Jordan Love in his first year as the starting quarterback. None of that mattered. Dak Prescott threw two interceptions, including a pick-six that helped build a 27-0 Green Bay lead, earning Love his first playoff win.

Welcome back, Mike: McCarthy's return to Lambeau

In Mike McCarthy's first two seasons as the Cowboys coach, Dallas didn't face Green Bay. So, the 2022 meeting was his first trip back to Lambeau Field since the Packers fired him in 2018.

articles.headline: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, keep James Wiseman ahead of opener
articles.description: The Knicks are waiving Bruce Brown and keeping James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: ニックス、ブルース・ブラウンを放出、ジェームズ・ウィズマンは開幕に向けて残留
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが報じたところによると、ニックスはレギュラーシーズン開幕を控え、ブルース・ブラウンを放出する一方で、ジェームズ・ウィズマンをロスターに留めることを決定した。
articles.body:
The New York Knicks waived Bruce Brown and will keep James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener.

Brown was one of several players on non-guaranteed deals vying for one of New York's final two available roster spots. Tony Bradley, Ochai Agbaji and Drew Eubanks were all also waived in recent days.

Wiseman appeared in all four of the Knicks' preseason games and impressed in 24 minutes vs. the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday, when he scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.

 

According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, the Knicks could have kept Brown and Wiseman, but because they are only $3.2 million below their self-imposed hard cap at the second apron, retaining both players would've been difficult.  

Wiseman, 25, will join Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond in New York's center rotation. The reigning NBA champions lost key reserve big man Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics this past summer via free agency.

The Knicks begin the NBA's regular season Tuesday, when they host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.headline: 76ers, needing frontcourt help, convert 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall to two-way contract
articles.description: The 76ers, dealing with injuries in the frontcourt, have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract.
articles.headlineJa: フロントコートの補強を必要とする76ers、7フィート6インチのタコ・フォールとツーウェイ契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: フロントコートでの怪我に悩まされている76ersは、センターのタコ・フォールをツーウェイ契約に切り替えた。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, the team announced Saturday.

Last month, the Sixers signed the 7-foot-6 center to an Exhibit 10 deal, and injuries to the frontcourt likely led to Fall getting this spot.

Ariel Hukporti, projected to be the Sixers' backup center, suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in the preseason. Center Adem Bona, potentially the next man up, has been sidelined with a foot injury, and Dominick Barlow has battled back soreness that kept him out of the preseason.

Fall hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season, when he was with the Cleveland Cavaliers. This will be his fourth season in the NBA. He played his first two in Boston with new Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Fall, 30, most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association.

articles.headlineJa: ジェームズとエンビード、76ersのプレシーズン最終戦に出場、「まだリズムを掴もうとしているところ」
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜夜のセルティックス戦（120-125で敗戦）を欠場したVJ・エッジコムが不在の中、76ersのニック・ナース監督は、レブロン・ジェームズとジョエル・エンビードがプレシーズン最多の出場時間を記録するなど、今シーズンのチーム像を最も具体的に示す形となった。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season.

The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets, finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​

He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed."

Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward.

"We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell.

"We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect."

The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

articles.headline: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa injures ankle during Wizards' preseason finale
articles.description: First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Wizards' preseason finale after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.
articles.headlineJa: ドラフト1位指名のAJ・ディバンツァ、ウィザーズのプレシーズン最終戦で足首を負傷
articles.descriptionJa: 全体1位指名のAJ・ディバンツァが、ウィザーズのプレシーズン最終戦で不自然な着地により足首を負傷して途中交代した。今後、詳細な検査を受ける予定。
articles.body:
First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Washington Wizards' preseason finale Friday after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes that Dybantsa had suffered a mild ankle sprain but that the decision to keep him out for the rest of the game was more precautionary.

"We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks.
